measurement_protocol.description: The measurement this cycle declared for its own outcome, verbatim from PlanState. Progress is judged against this and not against completion; when it has not been run, progress is unproven and no wearable reading substitutes for it.

review_frame.description: The calendar coordinates a review is framed on. The athlete's week is Monday to Sunday; every other window in this context is a rolling span ending at as_of, so a review framed on those would answer about the last seven days rather than about the week they trained. Dates only -- nothing here judges the training in them.

cycle_day.description: 1-based day of the declared cycle at as_of, uncapped: a value past the cycle length says the declared window has run out, which is when the measurement protocol comes due. Null before the cycle opens.

unavailable_days.description: Weekdays the athlete stated they cannot train. A separate statement, not the complement of available_days: naming a lost day confirms nothing about the others.

availability_source.description: Who stated the availability above: this turn's request, the athlete's stored evidence, or neither.

baseline_evidence.description: Each athlete_baseline field's claim beside recent evidence already in this context, with how many observations back it -- so 'once' and 'four weeks running' are distinguishable without re-deriving them. One row per scalar field, one row per strength movement, through the same row shape. Carries no verdict: no stale flag, no confidence score, no suggested value; which side is right is coaching judgment. observed is null when the window holds nothing for the field; a null window on a strength row means no strength source was read at all.

cycle_session.description: One session this cycle prescribed whose day has passed, rebuilt from the commit chain, with whatever came back for it beside the prescription. Rest days are not in it. A record for the coach to read: no completion percentage, and no status derived from a ratio. 'Planned but not done' is this record read for an absent activity; 'started but unfinished' is the same row read against the prescription. Per-set strength truth is not copied here — it stays in strength_execution, joined by date.

week_start.description: The Monday of the natural week this session was scheduled in, so a cycle groups into the weeks the athlete trained rather than into seven-day slices counted back from today.

match_status.description: The PlanState value verbatim, from the last version that carried this session.

activity_evidence.description: Why the activity is what it is. Only 'none_found' — this build read that day and nothing of that sport attached — is evidence about the athlete. 'other_activity_same_day' means that sport was trained that day but attached to another session or to none, a matching question and not a missed session. 'outside_evidence_window' means the day is older than anything this build read.

cycle_session_activity.description: The activity deterministic matching attached to this session, in the same terms recent_actuals uses. match_confidence carries how firm the attachment is; 'probable' is a same-day, same-sport candidate, not a completion.

average_pace_sec_per_km.description: Averaged across the whole activity, warm-up and recoveries included. On a session that prescribed structure it is not a reading of the work; segment_execution is.

average_hr.description: Averaged across the whole activity, warm-up and recoveries included. On a session that prescribed structure it is not a reading of the work; segment_execution is.

segment_execution.description: Per-segment execution for recent runs, exactly as the provider grouped them. Segments are not aligned to the session's prescribed steps: a prescribed warm-up plus five reps plus a cool-down can come back as fifteen segments with the warm-up split across two, so which segments are the work is a reading of the numbers and belongs to the coach. Null when no source could produce it.

index.description: Position in the provider's own ordering, so a coach can refer to a segment without renumbering it.

provider_type.description: What the provider called this segment. Not a claim that a WORK segment is the prescribed work -- on a real interval session almost every segment comes back typed WORK.

movement_history.description: Strength evidence grouped by movement, with what was prescribed on the same date beside it. The same figures strength_execution carries, pivoted from 'what was lifted that day' to 'how has this movement been going' -- the question a next prescription turns on. Carries no verdict: no completion rate, no progression score, no direction flag. Null when no strength evidence resolved to a movement.

display_name.description: The athlete's own word for the movement, from the baseline entry that anchors it. Null rather than the canonical key, which is an internal handle.

prescribed.description: Null means no plan prescribed this movement on this date -- trained off-plan, or older than the plan record. A list because one day can prescribe the same movement in parts.

baseline_evidence_threshold_pace_row.description: The fastest whole-run average pace observed, with the run's distance beside it. A whole-run average spans warm-up and recoveries; the label is what keeps it from reading as a threshold measurement.

baseline_evidence_max_hr_row.description: The highest whole-activity average heart rate observed, any sport. An average bounds a maximum from below; it never measures one.

baseline_evidence_easy_hr_row.description: The range of average heart rates across runs this context already classified easy. The range is reported, not the excess over the ceiling.

baseline_evidence_weekly_volume_row.description: Observed running per natural Monday-to-Sunday week, newest first, only weeks the evidence window holds in full. Zero runs is a statement about this window of the feed, not a claim the athlete trained nothing.

through.description: The last date this week's tally includes. Before the week's Sunday it states the week is still open; km null means a run in the week carries no recorded distance, so the total is unknown rather than zero.

baseline_evidence_strength_row.description: One strength movement's written baseline beside the loads it was actually worked at -- movement_history's occurrences grouped once more, by the day's top working weight (or least assistance, the heavier direction for an assisted lift).
